comments.text:
Unfortunately, not much can be done:

If instead the senator dies before the term expires, the seat becomes vacant upon death, and the applicable state vacancy procedures govern what happens for the remainder of the term.

The more difficult period is between the onset of permanent incapacity and the expiration of the term. During that interval, if the senator remains legally alive but cannot perform any duties, there is no automatic constitutional mechanism to replace them because of incapacity alone.

This is one reason some constitutional scholars have suggested that Congress or the states should consider an amendment or statute creating a process for determining when a member of Congress is permanently incapacitated. Unlike the presidency, where the Twenty-fifth Amendment addresses incapacity, Congress has no comparable framework for its own members.
